newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil basically steady in Europe despite data.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil basically steady in Europe despite data.

text.p: The palm oil sector in Europe was basically steady overall, despite poorer than expected Malaysian June 1-25 palm oil exports data from cargo surveyor Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) Malaysia.
SGS estimated Malaysia's palm oil exports for June 1-25 at 510,578 tonnes against 547,382 tonnes for May 1-25.
At midday palm oils were unchanged to $2.50 lower.

"With the poor export data, losses on the Chicago soybean oil futures overnight and Egypt not purchasing the full amount of palm oil it tendered for, you would expect prices to have fallen further than they have," one trader said.
"I think the main reason they haven't is a lack of interest in doing business at present, possible due to many traders being absent due to holidays," she added.
Business was light and mostly confined to 1-7 July period, at which RBD palm, olein and stearin fetched $514, $560 and $394 respectively. Olein also sold Aug/Sep at $549.
Soy oil also reflected the general unwillingness to do anything constructive despite lower levels in Chicago. At the end of the morning it stood unchanged to 0.50 guilders down.
Rape oil was unchanged and like soy oil tradeless. Lauric oils were another untraded sector but managed to post gains of $2.50 to $5. --Stephen Grainger +44 171 542 8074.
